learningObjectives: Implement structured logging for Python applications.
Distinguish logs, metrics, and traces in application monitoring.
Design an observability workflow for diagnosing application issues.

activities.title: Observability Map
activities.instruction: Explore the three major observability signals and their purposes.

content.concept: Logs describe events, metrics measure numerical behavior over time, and traces show the path of a request across components.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: Timestamped records of application events, errors, and useful contextual information.
Numerical measurements such as request count, latency, CPU usage, or memory usage.
Records the path and timing of a request as it travels through application components.
Notifications triggered when monitored conditions cross defined thresholds or rules.
A visual view that presents important metrics and service health information.

activities.title: Python Log Anatomy
activities.instruction: Click each part of the logging example to understand its role.

content.concept: Python's logging module supports severity levels and structured contextual information that can help diagnose application behavior.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: Creates or retrieves a logger associated with the current Python module.
Records an informational event and attaches contextual data such as a user ID.
Records an error with exception information, useful when diagnosing failures inside an exception handler.

activities.title: Observability Signal Selector
activities.instruction: Choose the signal that best answers the question.

content.concept: Logs, metrics, and traces complement each other. Selecting the appropriate signal makes troubleshooting more efficient.

activities.title: Monitoring Workflow Builder
activities.instruction: Build a workflow for detecting and diagnosing an application failure.

content.concept: An effective observability workflow moves from detecting an abnormal condition to investigating evidence, identifying the cause, and taking corrective action.
